html:
Sam Nujoma was the founding president of Namibia, who led SWAPO through the liberation struggle and governed the country from independence in 1990 until 2005.

Born in the Ovambo north, he worked on the railways in Windhoek and organised against the contract labour system. In 1960 he became president of SWAPO and went into exile, where he led the armed struggle and the campaign at the United Nations for 30 years.

He returned in 1989 and was elected president. His government chose reconciliation with the white minority and kept a market economy, while SWAPO came to dominate politics. He served three terms, after the constitution was changed for him. Namibia calls him the father of the nation, the heir of resistance led by Hendrik Witbooi.
sum: Sam Nujoma was the founding president of Namibia, who led SWAPO through the liberation struggle and governed the country from independence in 1990 until 2005.
